evidence: Graesse, Orbis Latinus (1861), index s.v. Schottland: Caledonia, Scotia
terms.comment: In late antiquity Scōtia meant Ireland (Isid. 14.6.6, Lewis & Short s.v. Scoti). A country takes a preposition: in Scōtiam (to), in Scōtiā (in), ē Scōtiā (from).

evidence: Graesse, Orbis Latinus (1861), index s.v. Schottland: Caledonia, Scotia
terms.comment: The ancient name of the Highlands, used for all Scotland.

scotia.against: Lewis & Short scŏtia, another word (a moulding)
scotia.html: Lewis & Short s.v. Scōti: Scōtia, the land of the Scots, with the long vowel of the people’s name.

sources: Lewis & Short: Scoti
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio, geographical section, with the authorities it cites (cited as M-O s.v.).

J. G. Th. Graesse, Orbis Latinus (Dresden, 1861), German–Latin index, read in the scan at archive.org (the 1909 edition at columbia.edu could not be reached page by page); its forms are post-classical unless Lewis & Short has them.
